newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-CORK BOUNCES BACK WITH SUNDAY BEST 6-21.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CORK BOUNCES BACK WITH SUNDAY BEST 6-21.

text.p: England pace bowler Dominic Cork bounced back from a four-month injury absence with his best Sunday League figures of six for 21 to fire Derbyshire to an eight-wicket win over Glamorgan.
Cork, who was sidelined for four months and had a hernia operation just six weeks ago, helped to rout Glamorgan for 103 at Chesterfield in the 40 overs competition.
Then he scored 33 as Derbyshire cruised to victory at 106 for two with 22.5 overs to spare.

"I'm not even thinking about a schedule for playing for England at the moment," insisted Cork. "Performance and fitness will dictate that but obviously if I keep producing figures like this, I would have a chance of getting back in the frame."
Ex-England batsman Neil Fairbrother eased Lancashire two points clear at the top of the table with a match-winning innings against Hampshire at Southampton.
Fairbrother scored 88 from 104 balls, hitting seven boundaries, to carry Lancashire to success at 214 for six after Hampshire made 210 for nine, their Australian opener Matthew Hayden hammering 55.
Essex stayed second after they tied with Worcestershire in a gripping finish at Chelmsford.
David Leatherdale earned Worcestershire a share of the points by bowling Ashley Cowan off the last ball with both sides having scored 217 from their 40 overs.
Earlier, Australian Tom Moody struck 59 from 68 balls, an effort which included four sixes, before he became one of compatriot Stuart Law's wickets in his four for 37.

Steve Rhodes established a league record when he claimed the second of his two victims behind the stumps. It took the Worcestershire wicketkeeper's total dismissals to 258, beating the previous best of 257 held by Yorkshire's David Bairstow.
Pakistani Mohammad Akram produced a telling display of fast bowling to set up Northamptonshire's fifth victory of the season, against title holders Surrey at Northampton.
Akram claimed four for 19 from his eight overs as Surrey were held to 206 for seven, Jason Ratcliffe playing the major role with 82 from 89 deliveries.
Northants reached their target at 208 for five in the final over thanks to an undefeated Sunday best of 81 from Tony Penberthy.
